repo.description:
### Summary The endpoints that save the git source of an application (`application.saveGithubProvider`, `saveGitlabProvider`, `saveBitbucketProvider`, `saveGiteaProvider`, `saveGitProvider`, and `application.update`) and of a compose service (`compose.update`) only call `checkServicePermissionAndAccess(..., { service: ["create"] })`. They then write the posted `githubId`, `gitlabId`, `bitbucketId`, `giteaId` or `customGitSSHKeyId` straight into the row. Nothing checks that the caller may use that provider, that it belongs to the caller's organization, or that it is shared. The provider routers (`github.one`, `getGithubRepositories`, `getGithubBranches`, ...) do call `assertGitProviderAccess`, and `application.one` / `compose.one` call `canEditDeployGitSource` (added in PR #4570) but only to return a `hasGitProviderAccess = false` flag for the UI. At deploy time the clone helpers load the provider by id with no organization or ownership check and clone with its token, app credentials or private key. A member who may edit a service can therefore switch it to a provider that was not shared with them and deploy any repository that this provider's credentials can read. With the `static` build type the cloned files are served by the app's own nginx, so the member can read them. ### Details Dokploy `canary`, `1048bcb113` (2026-11-09, the current HEAD; the cited files `application.ts`, `compose.ts`, `git-provider.ts`, `utils/providers/github.ts` and `services/application.ts` are identical upstream on 2026-11-11). Paths are under the repository root. Line numbers are for this commit. **Save endpoints without a provider check** (`apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/application.ts`) - `:543-567` `saveGithubProvider`: `checkServicePermissionAndAccess(ctx, input.applicationId, { service: ["create"] })`, then `updateApplication(..., { githubId: input.githubId, owner, repository, branch, ... })`. - `:569-594` `saveGitlabProvider` (`gitlabId`), `:596-620` `saveBitbucketProvider` (`bitbucketId`), `:622-646` `saveGiteaProvider` (`giteaId`), `:669-692` `saveGitProvider` (`customGitSSHKeyId`): the same two steps. - `:760-784` `update` (`apiUpdateApplication`): the schema is `createSchema.partial().omit({ serverId, environmentId })` (`packages/server/src/db/schema/application.ts:549-554`), so `githubId`, `gitlabId`, `giteaId`, `bitbucketId`, `customGitSSHKeyId`, `registryId` and `sourceType` can all be posted. Only `buildServerId` gets an extra check (`:766-773`). `...rest` goes to `updateApplication`. - `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/compose.ts:200-212` `update` (`apiUpdateCompose`, `packages/server/src/db/schema/compose.ts:274-281`, same `omit` of `serverId` and `environmentId` only): `updateCompose(input.composeId, input)` writes `githubId`, `gitlabId`, `bitbucketId`, `giteaId`, `customGitSSHKeyId` and `sourceType`. The compose UI uses this endpoint for all of its git providers (for example `save-github-provider-compose.tsx:151-156`). - `packages/server/src/services/application.ts:147-160` `updateApplication` and `services/compose.ts:212-226` `updateCompose` set whatever they get. - `checkServicePermissionAndAccess` (`packages/server/src/services/permission.ts:349-367`) only proves that the service is in the caller's organization, that the caller holds `service: create`, and that non-owner/admin members have the service in `accessedServices`. It says nothing about the provider. **How a provider id relates to its owner and organization** - `applications.githubId` / `gitlabId` / `giteaId` / `bitbucketId` reference `github.githubId` etc. (`db/schema/application.ts:212-223`), and each of those rows has `gitProviderId` -> `git_provider` with `organizationId`, `userId` and `sharedWithOrganization` (`db/schema/git-provider.ts:19-38`). The save endpoints only need the foreign key to exist. - Because only existence is needed, an id from another organization is also accepted by the save endpoints, and `findGithubById` and the other `find*ById` helpers load by primary key without an organization filter (`services/github.ts:49-63`). The id is a nanoid, so a cross-organization use needs the id from somewhere else. The same-organization case below needs no guessing. **Siblings that do check** - `routers/github.ts:27-31` (`one`), `:44-48` (`getGithubRepositories`), `:52-56` (`getGithubBranches`), `:110` (`update`), and the same in `gitlab.ts`, `gitea.ts`, `bitbucket.ts`: `assertGitProviderAccess(ctx.session, provider.gitProvider)` (`packages/server/src/services/git-provider.ts:134-153`), which refuses another organization's provider and one that is not in `getAccessibleGitProviderIds` (own, shared with the organization, or assigned to the member under a licence). - `application.ts:259-308` (`one`) and `compose.ts:150-190` (`one`): `canEditDeployGitSource(gitProviderId, ctx.session)` (`git-provider.ts:52-76`) returns true for an organization owner, otherwise only when the provider's `userId` is the caller or `sharedWithOrganization` is true. When it is false these endpoints only set `hasGitProviderAccess = false` and `unauthorizedProvider`. The function's comment states the intent: only the owner, or a user with an own or shared provider, may change the git settings of an existing deploy. A search of the repository finds it called from these two places only (plus its unit test). PR #4570 (merged 2026-06-07) introduced it, replacing a `userId`-only comparison in the same two read endpoints. None of the save endpoints use it. - `routers/git-provider.ts:32-40` and `github.ts` (`githubProviders`) list only accessible providers, so the UI does not offer a provider the user cannot use. The server side of the save does not enforce the same list. **Deploy uses the credential without a check** - `packages/server/src/services/application.ts:178-225` `deployApplication`: for `sourceType` github / gitlab / gitea / bitbucket / git it calls the matching clone helper with the application row, then `getBuildCommand`. - `utils/providers/github.ts:224-236` `cloneGithubRepository`: `findGithubById(githubId)`, an installation token from the provider's app id and private key, then `git clone ... https:////.git` with that token. `owner`, `repository` and `branch` come from the service row, which the caller controls. `gitlab.ts:159-176` uses `gitlab.accessToken`, `gitea.ts:180` uses `giteaProvider.accessToken`, `bitbucket.ts:115-129` builds the clone URL from the stored app password, and `utils/providers/git.ts:50-54` and `:81-84` write `sshKey.privateKey` to a temporary key file for `customGitSSHKeyId`. None of them compare the provider's organization, user or sharing flag with the user who saved the source. `services/compose.ts:257` does the same for compose services. **Getting the content out** - Build type `static` (`utils/builders/static.ts`, saved with `application.saveBuildType` under the same `service: create` check, `application.ts:518-541`) writes a Dockerfile `FROM nginx:alpine` with `COPY ${publishDirectory || "."} .` and a `.dockerignore` that excludes only `.git`, `.env`, `Dockerfile` and `.dockerignore`. The cloned repository is built into the image and served by nginx. With a domain on the app (`domain.create` needs `domain: create`, which the member role has), the files are readable over HTTP. `publishDirectory` and `buildType` are also under the member's control. - The deployment log (readable with `deployment: read`) shows the clone line `Cloning Repo //.git` and git errors, which also tells the member whether the repository exists and is reachable with that credential. - For compose services the member does not choose the compose file's contents, so reading files out is less direct. The change of credential is the same. **Who can reach it and how they get the id** - The caller needs `service: create` on the service (for the free roles `canCreateServices`, `permission.ts:160-166`, or a custom role with the enterprise access control) and the service in `accessedServices`. Owner and admin pass `checkServicePermissionAndAccess` for every service in the organization. `canEditDeployGitSource` is true only for an owner, so an admin is also affected against a provider that someone else created and did not share. - Case 1, no guessing: the service already uses a provider that the caller may not edit. `application.one` / `compose.one` return the row including `githubId` (and `gitlabId`, ...) to anyone with read access, together with `hasGitProviderAccess: false`. The caller posts `saveGithubProvider` with the same `githubId` and a different `owner` / `repository` / `branch`, so the application now clones another repository with that provider's credential. This is the situation the flag from PR #4570 detects but the save does not refuse. - Case 2: the id of another provider in the same organization that is not attached to any service the caller can read. Providers are listed to a member only if they are accessible (`getAccessibleGitProviderIds`), so the id is not enumerable and has to be learned some other way. - Case 3, Dokploy Cloud or a multi-organization install: the nanoid of a provider in another organization. Not guessable, so this needs a leak of the id. **Not the same as published issues** GHSA-wx75 and GHSA-hg9j concern reading secrets of a provider through the read endpoints, and PR #5329 concerns the provider's own update re-pointing a foreign key. This report is about the save side of a service: the provider is chosen by a user who was never given it, and the deploy then uses its credential. ### Proof of concept Setup (a test instance you control, not a public one; use a test GitHub App or token and a private test repository): an organization with an owner `admin`; a member `dev` with `canCreateServices` and access (`accessedServices`) to one application `app1`. `admin` has created a GitHub provider `P` (a GitHub App installed on the test account that owns a private repository `testorg/secret-repo`) and has not shared it with the organization. `secret-repo` contains a file `private.txt` with a marker string. `admin` has connected `app1` to `P` with some other test repository, so that `dev` can read `P`'s `githubId` from `app1`. 1. As `dev`, `GET /api/trpc/application.one?input={"json":{"applicationId":""}}`. The response has `githubId` = `P` and `hasGitProviderAccess: false`. As `dev`, `github.one` for `P` and the repository list for `P` are refused by `assertGitProviderAccess`. 2. As `dev`: `POST /api/trpc/application.saveGithubProvider` with `{"json":{"applicationId":"","githubId":"

","owner":"testorg","repository":"secret-repo","branch":"main","buildPath":"/","triggerType":"push","enableSubmodules":false,"watchPaths":[]}}`. The call returns `true`. No provider check runs. 3. As `dev`: `POST application.saveBuildType` with `buildType: "static"` and `publishDirectory: "."` (the other fields as the UI sends them), and `POST domain.create` for `app1` with a test host (or use whatever port mapping the test instance allows). 4. As `dev`: `POST application.deploy`. The deployment log shows `Cloning Repo github.com/testorg/secret-repo.git ...` and a successful build. `GET http:///private.txt` returns the marker string of the private repository. 5. For the other providers repeat step 2 with `saveGiteaProvider` / `saveGitlabProvider` / `saveBitbucketProvider` and a provider of the matching kind. For an SSH key, `saveGitProvider` with `customGitUrl` set to a test repository that accepts a test deploy key and `customGitSSHKeyId` set to the id of an SSH key created by `admin`. 6. Control: the same posts from a user without `service: create` on `app1`, or without access to `app1`, fail with the existing permission errors, so the only missing check is the one on the provider. To undo on the test instance, reconnect `app1` with `disconnectGitProvider` as `admin` and delete the domain. (Static review. Not yet run against a live instance.) ### Impact A user who may edit a service (for the free roles, a member given `canCreateServices` and the service) but who was not given a git provider or SSH key can use that credential anyway. With a GitHub App, GitLab or Gitea token, or Bitbucket app password that can read private repositories, they can deploy those repositories as their own service and read the files through a static build on a domain. The credential itself (token, private key) is not returned to them. Access is to every repository the credential can read, not only the one the owner had in mind, because `owner` and `repository` are chosen by the caller. An SSH key attached to a service is used for any URL the caller sets. Preconditions that limit this: the caller must already be allowed to edit a service and have it in their accessible services. They must know a provider id: either the provider is already attached to a service they can read (the case the flag from PR #4570 describes), or they got the id of another provider elsewhere. Where only owners hold `service: create`, there is no practical impact. Providers shared with the whole organization are usable by design. Suggested severity: Moderate, CVSS 3.1 `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` (6.5). The confidentiality rating assumes the unshared provider can reach private repositories that the caller cannot otherwise read. CWE-639 (a user-controlled provider id with no ownership check) and CWE-862 (missing authorization on the save). ### Suggested fix - In `saveGithubProvider`, `saveGitlabProvider`, `saveBitbucketProvider`, `saveGiteaProvider` and `saveGitProvider`, load the provider and call `assertGitProviderAccess(ctx.session, provider.gitProvider)` when the id changes. For an id the service already has, call `canEditDeployGitSource` before changing `owner`, `repository` or `branch`. For `customGitSSHKeyId` check that the key belongs to the caller's organization and that the caller may use it. - Do the same in `application.update` and `compose.update`, or remove the provider and key fields (`githubId`, `gitlabId`, `giteaId`, `bitbucketId`, `customGitSSHKeyId`, `sourceType`) from `apiUpdateApplication` and `apiUpdateCompose`, as is already done for `serverId` and `environmentId`. - Consider checking the provider's organization in the clone helpers as well, so a row written before the fix cannot deploy with a credential its editor was never given. ### Method Read-only review of the source at `1048bcb113` (`canary`, 2026-11-09), with the cited files compared with upstream `canary` on 2026-11-11 and PR #4570 read with `gh api`. AI tools were used to find the candidate and to read the cited code. Not yet reproduced on a running instance.
repo.summary: Saving the git source of an application or compose does not check access to the git provider: a member can point their service at another user's unshared GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket provider or SSH key and clone private repositories with it
